interactions.summary: The class develops better answers to the geolocation problem: exact detail measures progress, gives the reader a map for imagination, and anticipates Renaissance perspective by making the poem spatially inhabitable.

claims.claim: Jiang accepts progress-tracking as one strong reason for exact geolocation: measurement lets the reader and pilgrim feel movement rather than abstraction.
A student calls the mountain description a treasure map for imagination, and Jiang embraces that image as a way to explain why detail matters.
This treasure-map logic links Dante to the Renaissance because perspective and dense physical detail teach the reader how to imagine a world more fully.

signature_moments.moment: Mount Purgatory becomes a treasure map for imagination rather than a static theological diagram.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the most memorable bridge between geography, art, and readerly participation.

chronology_notes.note: The open question about Purgatory's exact location becomes a positive theory of imaginative realism: detail measures progress and trains spatial vision.
